# Phantom

> Open-source workbench for running coding agents, coordinating a fleet, and reviewing their work, through a CLI (`phm`, alias `ashlr`), an MCP gateway, and a web console. This root file is the repository entry point for agents; the full page index is [docs/llms.txt](docs/llms.txt).

Mission: chasing open-source RSI (recursive self-improvement). Phantom and its companion tools aim to form a fully autonomous, code-first, agent-native software factory. Agents pick work, open pull requests, merge them and ship releases through the sanctioned workflow; the human owner acts as a passive board member, needed only for passwords, 2FA, device approvals and payments. Strategy: [recursive self-improvement and an open fleet](docs/strategy/RECURSIVE-SELF-IMPROVEMENT-AND-OPEN-FLEET-2026-11.md).

Ecosystem: Phantom is the hub. Separately installed companions are phantom-secrets (secrets), ashlr-plugin (token-efficient agent tools), Locus (identity scoping), lexicon (vocabulary), ashlr-md (Markdown review) and ashlr-stack (service provisioning). A registered companion MCP server is not proof that it is ready. See [companion setup](docs/COMPANIONS.md) and the [ecosystem map](docs/ECOSYSTEM-MAP.md).

## Install and first run

Requires Node.js 22.15.0 or newer and Git. `phm` and `ashlr` are the same program.

```sh
npm install -g @ashlr/phantom
phm --version
phm docs --agent --json
phm verse --no-open --json
```

`phm docs --agent --json` prints the installed command registry, which is the reference for your version. `phm verse` serves the console at `http://127.0.0.1:7777/verse/` and prints a read token; keep tokens private.

- [README](README.md): What Phantom is, its surfaces, the quickstart and the ecosystem table.
- [Quickstart](docs/QUICKSTART.md): Install Phantom, open the console, and make a first turn.
- [Claude, Cursor and Codex setup](docs/AGENT-MCP-CLI.md): Connect a coding agent through MCP and the CLI.
- [Full copy-paste reference](docs/llms-full.txt): Install, JSON commands, and MCP setup.

## How agents work on this repository

- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): The agent constitution. Agents may branch, commit, open pull requests, merge and dispatch releases through the sanctioned workflow; secret values, force-pushes, admin bypass, spending and messages to outsiders stay with the owner.
- [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md): Commands and rules for coding agents. Before a PR, run `node scripts/verify-changed.mjs` once in the foreground, then `npm run check:docs` and the affected tests.
- [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md): Conventions, hermetic tests and contract-first changes.
- [Agent operations](docs/AGENT-OPERATIONS.md): Cold-start checklist for building and operating Phantom from source.
- [Agent toolchain](docs/AGENT-TOOLCHAIN.md): Companion MCP servers declared in `.mcp.json`, with their limits and approval requirements.

## Fleet, routing and teams

- [Router gateway](docs/ROUTER-GATEWAY.md): `phm run --model auto "<prompt>" --json`, `phm router serve|models|pick|config --json`; loopback-only OpenAI-compatible endpoint and one CLI call over `routeSeat`. Preview with `phm router pick`.
- [Node router](docs/NODE-ROUTER.md): `phm node join|pull|plan|status --json`; computers join as nodes, jobs carry an owner scope, per-job leases with fencing tokens so no job runs twice.
- [Agent network](docs/AGENT-NETWORK.md): SSH multi-Mac node pool, join, worker, list/status, heartbeat, backup fencing and RPC JSON contract.
- [Team org](docs/AGENT-NETWORK.md#team-org): `phm org show|join|plan --json`; declarative org.toml of members, agents, lanes and contributed shares; opt-in per lane, plan within contributed limits, nothing private pooled.
- [Team invite, join and remove](docs/TEAM.md#invite-join-and-remove-a-teammate): `phm team invite <gh-user>`, `phm team join <invite>`, `phm team remove <gh-user> --json`; membership only, no credentials, each node keeps its own local auth, removal drains claims.
- [Queue tiers](docs/QUEUE.md#tier-values): router-queue `tier=` is `frontier`, `work`, `mid` or `fast`; queuegen and router-lint reject any other value (`standard` means `work`), since dispatchd skips unknown tiers silently.
- Dispatcher admission: `phm pool admission --json` reads the starvation signals and what dispatchd would decide about new claims right now; read-only.
- [Lane health](docs/LANE-HEALTH.md): `phm lanes health --json`, calls, error rate, p50 latency and deployed commit per lane over 12 h, with a stuck badge and phase age past a phase timeout.
- [Standing lane freshness](docs/FLEET-LANE-FRESHNESS.md): `phm fleet lane-slots --json`, observations during mirror prep, per-repo timeout and unknown capacity.
- [Provider capacity cards](docs/PROVIDER-CARDS.md): `phm resource --cards --json`, usage and burn-down per provider, unknown stays unknown.
- [oMLX on the small Macs](docs/OMLX-SMALL-MACS.md): `phm node lanes --json` plans an evidence-picked local model per RAM class; join/worker advertise `omlx`/`omlx-work` caps with kernel memory-pressure backoff; HF/oMLX caches are protected model roots.
- [Job cost breakdown](docs/JOB-COST.md): `phm job cost <id> --json` and loopback `GET /api/fleet/job/cost?id=<id>`; per-model-call tokens in/out, model and cost or 'unknown'.
- [Connector profiles](docs/CONNECTORS.md): `phm connectors add|list|remove|show|import --json`; declarative metadata and Phantom Secrets names, with explicit lane selectors and credential-safe import reports. `exec <id> --tool <tool> --lane <lane> -- <command>` launches with phantom-injected session tokens; `config --client claude|cursor|codex --lane <lane> --json` prints token-free client entries.
- [Learned skills](docs/SKILLS.md): `phm skills list --json`; reusable skills written after verified PR merges, scrubbed and size-capped, counts real or `unknown`.
